'''Richard Mansfield Dudley''' (July 28, 1938 – January 19, 2020)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.mit.edu/2020/richard-dudley-mit-mathematics-professor-emeritus-dies-0218 |title=Richard Dudley, professor emeritus of mathematics, dies at 81 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=February 18, 2020 |website=MIT News |access-date=July 14, 2020}}</ref> was an American mathematician. He was Professor of Mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1967 to his retirement in 2015.<ref name="MMA"/>

== Education and career ==
Dudley was born in [[Cleveland, Ohio]]. He earned his BA at [[Harvard College]] and received his PhD at [[Princeton University]] in 1962 under the supervision of [[Edward Nelson]] and [[Gilbert Hunt]].  He was a [[Putnam Fellow]] in 1958. He was an instructor and assistant professor at [[University of California, Berkeley]] between 1962 and 1967, before moving to [[MIT]] as a professor in mathematics, where he stayed from 1967 until 2015, when he retired.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web |title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |access-date=December 9, 2021 |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312205244/http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He died on January 19, 2020, following a long illness.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Richard M. Dudley {{!}} MIT Mathematics|url=https://math.mit.edu/about/history/obituaries/dudley.php|access-date=2021-02-20|website=math.mit.edu}}</ref>

== Research ==
His work mainly concerned fields of probability,<ref>{{Cite book|last=Rojo|first=Javier|title=Selected Works of E.L. Lehmann|date=2016|publisher=Springer-Verlag|location=New York|isbn=978-1-4939-5104-8|edition=Softcover reprintF=|oclc=959948252}}</ref> mathematical statistics, and machine learning, with highly influential contributions to the theory of Gaussian processes and empirical processes. He published over a hundred papers in peer-reviewed journals and authored several books. His specialty was [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]], especially [[empirical process]]es.<ref>{{cite journal|title=A Conversation with Dick Dudley|last1=Koltchinskii |first1=Vladimir |last2= Nickl|first2=Richard|authorlink2=Richard Nickl|last3=Rigollet|first3=Philippe| journal=[[Statistical Science]]|volume=34|issue=1|pages=169–175|year=2019|doi=10.1214/18-STS678 |s2cid=145989186 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/statistical-science/volume-34/issue-1/A-Conversation-with-Dick-Dudley/10.1214/18-STS678.pdf}}</ref> He is often noted for [[Dudley's theorem|his results]] on the so-called ''Dudley entropy integral''.<ref>{{cite journal |first=R. M. |last=Dudley |title=The sizes of compact subsets of Hilbert space and continuity of Gaussian processes |journal=[[Journal of Functional Analysis]] |volume=1 |issue=3 |pages=290–330 |year=1967 |doi=10.1016/0022-1236(67)90017-1 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=R. M. |last=Dudley |title=Uniform Central Limit Theorems |series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics |volume=63 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge, UK |year=1999 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/mathematics/18-465-topics-in-statistics-statistical-learning-theory-spring-2007/lecture-notes/ |title=Exposition of statistical learning theory }}, including Dudley's entropy integral.</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>
